visuals: A vast expanse of the Sahara Desert in Morocco with rolling orange sand dunes under a clear sky. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: The geography here is super cool. It’s like nature rolled out every type of land it could think of! Sandy deserts in the south.

visuals: The snow-capped Atlas Mountains in Morocco under a clear, bright sky. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Snowy mountains in the middle.

visuals: A breezy Atlantic beach in Morocco with waves crashing on the shore. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And breezy beaches in the north.

visuals: The snow-capped peaks of the Atlas Mountains in Morocco with rocky hiking trails and pine trees. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Let’s check out the Atlas Mountains! They spread across Morocco and are filled with beautiful trails and mountain wildlife. If you're lucky and it's winter, you might even have a snowball fight!

visuals: A historic stone statue of a Barbary lion in Morocco. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Guess what animal once symbolized Moroccan royalty? The Barbary lion! It’s now extinct in the wild, but statues keep its spirit alive.

visuals: An illustration of a powerful Barbary lion in a rocky Moroccan landscape. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And stories keep its spirit alive.

visuals: A dromedary camel walking through the Sahara Desert dunes in Morocco. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: In the deserts, you’ll find camels shuffling through the sand.

visuals: A cute Fennec fox with large ears resting in the sandy desert of Morocco. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And Fennec foxes with HUGE ears staying cool in the heat. Cute and clever survival experts!

visuals: The peaceful Oudaya Kasbah in Rabat, Morocco, with its blue and white walls and a view of the sea. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: The capital of Morocco is called Rabat and has peaceful gardens, old forts, and breezy beaches. Wouldn’t you want to explore all that?

visuals: The massive Hassan II Mosque in Casablanca, Morocco, with its tall minaret stretching over the Atlantic Ocean. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Now zoom over to Casablanca, the biggest city, full of buzz and beauty. It’s home to the massive Hassan II Mosque, it's so big it even stretches over the ocean!

visuals: A narrow, ancient street in the Medina of Fes, Morocco, with its historic buildings and busy atmosphere. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And don’t miss Fes, one of the oldest university cities on Earth: over 1,000 years old!

visuals: Jemaa el-Fnaa square in Marrakech in Morocco bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: People in Morocco speak different languages, like Arabic and Amazigh, and lots also know French. So conversations can be a colorful mix!

visuals: Jemaa el-Fnaa square in Marrakech in Morocco bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: About 37 million people call Morocco home. That’s about the same as everyone in Canada!

visuals: A large traditional platter of Moroccan couscous topped with colorful vegetables and meat. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Now let’s talk food! Fridays are for family meals with couscous, fluffy and topped with veggies and meat. Yum!

visuals: A savory Moroccan tagine stew being cooked in a traditional pointed clay pot. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And there’s tagine, a savory stew cooked in a pointed clay pot. It smells amazing before you even take a bite.

visuals: A person in Morocco pouring sweet mint tea from a silver teapot held high above a small glass, with steam rising. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Thirsty yet? Try mint tea! It’s sweet, hot, and poured with flair—often from way up high! Sharing tea with guests is a big part of Moroccan hospitality.

visuals: Moroccan musicians playing traditional drums and guitars for a dancing crowd during a festival. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Let’s move to music and dance! Gnawa music blends African beats with Arab traditions, and it gets whole streets dancing during festivals. Are your feet tapping yet?

visuals: A Moroccan night festival with colorful lanterns, people in traditional kaftans, and a joyful atmosphere. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Big celebrations? Oh yes! During Eid or the Amazigh New Year, families gather, feast, and dance till late. Joy and togetherness light up the streets!

visuals: A soccer ball on a soccer field. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: In 2022, Morocco became the first African and Arab country to reach the men’s World Cup semifinals! The crowds went wild! Keep an eye on the Moroccan team; they recently made history by winning the 2025 FIFA Under 20 World Cup, becoming the first Arab nation and second African country to claim the title.

visuals: The blue streets of Chefchaouen in Morocco bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Speaking of sports, Morocco’s got champions like Achraf Hakimi.

visuals: Moroccan runner Hicham El Guerrouj racing on a professional track. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And Hicham El Guerrouj, the “King of the Mile.”

visuals: A beautiful narrow alley in Chefchaouen, Morocco, with its iconic blue-painted walls and potted flowers. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Wanna hear something fun? Some villages, like Chefchaouen, are completely painted blue! It has been suggested that the color keeps mosquitoes away. That’s a new way of repelling bugs I didn’t know!

visuals: The ancient mud-brick village of Aït Ben Haddou in Morocco, a UNESCO site nestled in the desert landscape. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And listen to this: there’s an ancient village made of mud in the middle of the desert. This impressive location was the setting for films like Gladiator, The Mummy, and Game of Thrones. Walking through it feels like another planet!
